leading_positions.synthesis: All six members list B044 as the sole prize part, with the same three laureates (Daniel J. Drucker, Jens Juul Holst, Svetlana Mojsov) and a physiology-centred citation. Citation wording differs slightly: some phrasings name the active peptide form, and some refer to incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Not shared: how confident members are in the three-name set, whether Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's drug-design work should be mentioned or credited, and how Joel Habener (not on the credited list) should be treated in the record. No member proposes a second prize part in the preferred configuration; second-part options appear only as alternatives or conditional remarks.

areas_of_agreement: All six preferred configurations are a single prize part for B044 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov.

Members describe B044 as a complete discovery chain from proglucagon processing and the active peptide to physiology and receptor biology, followed by large independent randomized outcome evidence in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. Several describe the field as mature and recognition as timely.
Every member names attribution as the main reservation for B044, and every member acknowledges that the supplied credited list may not capture the full historical record.

All six list B018 (CAR-T) among their alternatives; four (el-manira-abdel, linnarsson-sten, sandberg-rickard, svenningsson-per) list B001 (optogenetics) and two (perlmann-thomas, wahren-herlenius-marie) list B012 (unfolded protein response). These are alternatives, not preferred configurations.
Several members state that excluding Knudsen should be explicit and should reflect the three-person cap and the discovery framing, not a judgement that her work was minor.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus development: whether the prize should rest on GLP-1 physiology and the active peptide alone or also acknowledge the long-acting analogue work that made the therapy; members who exclude Knudsen differ on how costly that exclusion is.

Method versus discovery for B001: members differ on whether optogenetics is a physiology or medicine discovery, and whether the channelrhodopsin discovery and the neuronal application are separable achievements.

B012 versus B018 as the strongest option beyond B044: Wahren-Herlenius and Perlmann describe B012 as the cleanest pairing but with mainly conceptual impact so far, while others place B018 ahead because its clinical effect is established.
B013 (TOR): members disagree on the relative weight of Hall, Schreiber and Sabatini and on whether the clinical impact of rapalogs matches the conceptual importance.
Whether Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer work belongs in a CAR-specific citation for B018.
attribution_disputes: B044: credit for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is described as contested among Mojsov, Habener and others; Habener is not a credited ballot name, so members can vote only on supplied names. Members differ in how firmly they would keep Mojsov at full weight.
B044: the four-name credited list includes Knudsen, but all six preferred configurations leave her out, so the three-person cap forces an exclusion that members want stated in the record.

B001: six credited names (Bamberg, Boyden, Deisseroth, Hegemann, Miesenboeck, Nagel) for at most three seats; members note that a Deisseroth, Hegemann, Nagel trio would omit Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, and that a two-part design has been mentioned.

B018: Eshhar's early chimeric receptor work is outside the credited names, so some members consider that no fully fair CAR-T trio can be built from the supplied names; Rosenberg's inclusion is also questioned.
B012: Walter and Mori are a clean pair, but mammalian UPR branches (Ron, Harding, Kaufman) are outside the credited names.

B013: members disagree on whether Sabatini should be included, with some basing the question on scientific contribution and others on unverified professional-history concerns that a prize decision should not rest on.
maturity_disputes: B044 is described as mature by all members who address it, with no member arguing it is premature; one member notes that long-term safety of chronic incretin therapy is still accumulating, though not as a reason against the case.
B012: some members regard clinical translation after about three decades as limited or early, and disagree on whether a basic-mechanism prize should rank above a clinically proven one.
B001: clinical translation is described as limited so far, and timeliness is disputed: one member treats it as possibly overdue, while others say it can wait for a later year.
B018: described by several members as the most mature clinical alternative, with disagreement on whether this outweighs its attribution gap.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson-per (chair) discloses a postdoc with Paul Greengard and roughly twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy); he states no relationship with any credited name on this shortlist.

Perlmann-thomas discloses co-authorship with Per Svenningsson and a 2009 paper with Abdel El Manira, and collaborations with Ronald Evans and Johan Ericson who are not shortlist names; no recusal sought.
El-manira-abdel discloses a 2009 paper with Thomas Perlmann and a 2019 synthesis with Sten Grillner; none relate to a shortlisted ballot. He notes only field overlap with optogenetics (B001).
Linnarsson-sten and sandberg-rickard disclose prior co-authorship with each other (and Sandberg with Frisen), with none touching B044, B018 or B001.
Wahren-herlenius-marie discloses field overlap with CAR-T in autoimmune disease (B018) and cGAS-STING (B040) but no personal or institutional tie to any credited person.
All six members state that no specific conflict applies to the shortlisted candidates and none requests recusal.
questions_for_round2: For B044, should the citation and laureate set be confined to GLP-1 physiology and the active peptide (Drucker, Holst, Mojsov), or should the committee add or substitute a name for drug development such as Knudsen? If the latter, which of the three would be dropped given the cap?

What primary-record evidence do members rely on to decide whether Mojsov's contribution to the active peptide should be credited at full weight, and how should the committee record Habener's absence from the credited list?

Does any member want a second prize part alongside B044, and if so, which of B018, B012 or B001 and with what named set of three or fewer? Does a three-person cap across the whole prize leave any room for this?
For B018, can the committee defend a configuration without Eshhar, and does Rosenberg belong in a CAR-specific citation?

For B001, does the committee treat optogenetics as an eligible discovery rather than a tool, and if so, which separable achievement (channelrhodopsin function or neuronal application) would be recognized and who would be excluded?
For B012, would members who rank it behind B018 or B001 accept it as a second part, and how should the limited clinical translation weigh against its clean attribution?
If B013 is raised, what is the committee's basis for including or excluding Sabatini, restricted to documented scientific contribution?
summary.chair_observation: All six preferred configurations are identical in ballot and laureates, so round 1 shows convergence on B044 and its three-name set; disagreement lies in how to treat Knudsen and Habener, and in whether any second part is wanted. Alternatives differ more: B018 appears for all six, B001 for four and B012 for two. Members attach different reservations (attribution, method status, maturity) to each, and none of these positions has been tested beyond the written round-1 statements. As chair, I note that I hold the same preferred configuration as the other members and that I count only positions stated explicitly in the six files.
